output.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS customers_2024_not_2025
FROM marts.fct_orders o
WHERE LOWER(o.status) = 'completed'
  AND o.order_date >= DATE '2024-01-01'
  AND o.order_date < DATE '2025-01-01'
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM marts.fct_orders o2
    WHERE o2.customer_id = o.customer_id
      AND LOWER(o2.status) = 'completed'
      AND o2.order_date >= DATE '2025-01-01'
      AND o2.order_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
  );
output.explanation: This query counts the distinct customers who had at least one completed order dated in 2024 and no completed order dated in 2025. I took "completed" to mean orders whose status is 'completed', and the check ignores upper or lower case. I didn't use the is_revenue flag, because it may also cover other statuses such as shipped orders. If you meant "orders that count as revenue", replace the status check with is_revenue = true. Each year runs from January 1 to December 31, based on order_date.
